title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes (cote 64) study moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2 through the Legendre picture. E is a double cover of P^1 branched over a 4-point set Σ. t ∈ Σ is the branch point lying under the origin 0 of E. Write T = T_{E,0} for the tangent line at the origin and T_{Σ,t} for the relevant line attached to (Σ,t) on the base. Ramification gives the canonical isomorphism (5): T^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ,t}. The previous page records that T_{Σ,t} ≅ O_t(1)(ω), a twist of O_t(1) by a 2-element set ω = ω_J, i.e. a μ2-torsor depending on auxiliary data J.

The ambiguity. The naive candidate T_0 = O_t(1) has two equally natural isomorphisms T_0^{⊗2} → T_{Σ,t}, one for each element of ω. Twisting T_0 by a μ2-torsor does not help, because squaring kills the twist.

The fix. Twist instead by a μ4-torsor Q_0, the vertex set of a combinatorial square:
- (8): T_0 := O_t(1) ∧^{μ4} Q_0.
- (9): T_0^{⊗2} ≅ O_t(2) ∧^{μ2} DQ_0, where DQ_0 = Q_0/{±1} is the set of the two diagonals of the square.
- (11): the square comes equipped with orientations ≅ μ4^* = {i, −i} and a bijection between the diagonals of Q_0 and ω.
- (12): with these data, T_0^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ,t} canonically.

Definition on this page. A 'Legendre pinning' (épinglage de Legendre) of E, subordinate to the square Q_0, is an isomorphism κ: T_0 → T = T_{E,0} (13). It must be compatible with the given isomorphisms, i.e. make the triangle (14) commute: (5)∘κ^{⊗2} = (12). Such κ exist and there are exactly two, ±κ, forming a μ2-torsor.

Uniform version. One wants Q_0 fixed once and for all while E varies. But ω_J is not yet determined, because J is not. So a pinning is redefined as a pair (α, κ):
- α: DQ_0 = Q_0/{±1} → ω_J (15), an isomorphism;
- κ as in (13), satisfying (14).

What it serves. This rigidifies the tangent space at the origin of a Legendre-type elliptic curve, up to the automorphism −1. It is a step toward a canonical description of the moduli stack / Legendre λ-line with level-2-type structure plus a normalized invariant differential. The next page fixes Q_0 with a chosen oriented side, so that T_0 ⊗ O_t(−1) carries a pair of bases s_i, s_{−i} with s_{−i} = i·s_i.
errors: No mathematical error. Squaring induces μ4 → μ2 with kernel {±1}, so the pushed-out torsor is Q_0/{±1}, as claimed. In characteristic ≠ 2, isomorphisms of lines with a prescribed square-isomorphism are exactly ±κ, so 'exactly two' is correct.
Minor notational slip: (15) is written ∂Q_0 = Q_0{±1}; it should read DQ_0 = Q_0/{±1}.

ideas.what: Removing a 2-fold ambiguity in a square root of a line by twisting with a μ4-torsor rather than a μ2-torsor; the square of the twist is the μ2-torsor of diagonals Q_0/{±1}
ideas.modern_name: pushforward of torsors along μ4 → μ2 (squaring); square roots of line bundles / theta-characteristic-type rigidification
ideas.where_published: general torsor techniques appear in SGA/Giraud; this specific use is unpublished as far as known

ideas.what: Legendre pinning: an isomorphism κ: T_0 → T_{E,0} compatible with T_{E,0}^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ,t}, defined up to sign, i.e. normalizing the invariant differential of a Legendre-form curve modulo the automorphism −1
ideas.modern_name: rigidification of the tangent space / normalized invariant differential on the Legendre family (Γ(2)-level, modular forms of weight 1 for Γ(2)/Γ(4) type)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Legendre, Jacobi); modern moduli treatment Katz–Mazur, Deligne–Rapoport
ideas.where_published: unsure; possibly echoed in Esquisse d'un programme discussions of M_{1,1} and the Teichmüller tower, but not this formalism

ideas.what: Making the pinning uniform in families by adding the isomorphism α: Q_0/{±1} ≅ ω_J as part of the data
ideas.modern_name: moduli of elliptic curves with auxiliary level/torsor structure (fine moduli via rigidifying data)

missed.claim: A combinatorial-geometric ('square Q_0') rigidification of Legendre-form elliptic curves, intended to give canonical coordinates on the level-2 moduli stack in characteristic ≠ 2 with the tangent line normalized via a μ4-torsor. It is a coordinate-free account of why the normalization of the Legendre differential involves fourth roots of unity. The broader program in these notes is not developed in the literature under Grothendieck's name.
missed.quote: on appellera épinglage de Legendre de E, subordonnée au carré Q_0 ... un isomorphisme T = T_{E,0} ←κ T_0 ... Il y en a exactement deux
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mildly relevant to explicit descriptions of M_{1,1} and its level-2/level-4 covers, e.g. for Grothendieck–Teichmüller and dessins work on the Legendre line. Mathematically the content is equivalent to known level-structure/differential normalizations.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but essentially routine torsor-theoretic rigidification: twist by μ4 to resolve a sign ambiguity, then define pinnings up to ±1. The terminology 'épinglage de Legendre' and the square picture are unpublished details, but the mathematics is equivalent to standard level-structure and differential normalizations.
transcription_corrections: 'subordonnée au couple Q_0' is likely 'subordonné au carré Q_0'.
'Il y en exactement deux' should read 'Il y en a exactement deux, définis au signe près' (roughly).
'notion d'épinglage de E contenant d'un Q_0 donné' is likely 'en termes d'un Q_0 donné une fois pour toutes, pour E variable — mais alors ω = ω_J n'est pas encore déterminé'.
In diagram (14) the left vertical double line appears to be an identification mark; the arrows labelled (12) and (5) go to T_{Σ,t}.
